title: Reliability Pulse: SprintKit & Ops Bridge Notes (Q4 2026)
content:
Context:

This doc captures the SprintKit approach for running a multi-week Reliability Pulse focused on SLO stabilization, ops-bridge readiness, and three cross-functional pilots: live canary for model routing, prefix cache warmers, and per-route error-budget automation. Goal is a repeatable kit teams can adopt without heavy SRE overhead.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- We keep getting transient regressions across hosted/dedicated/private stacks that evade post-hoc analysis.
- Multiple teams have different SLO definitions and runbook practices; inconsistent incident response increases MTTI/MTTR.
- Need a lightweight, repeatable SprintKit that bundles cadence, checklists, dashboards, and short-run experiments to reduce error budget burn and codify handoffs.

Objectives (measurable):
1) Standardize SLO definitions for 3 critical product routes (text-gen, chat-stream, embeddings) and publish them in Confluence by sprint end.
2) Reduce weekly error-budget noise (alerts with >50% false positive rate) by 60% via dashboard tuning and alert threshold refinement.
3) Validate an automated failover policy for model-variant fallback in one customer-facing region (US-WEST) with canary traffic for 48 hours.
4) Onboard two product teams to the ops-bridge checklist and ensure each has a runbook, an owner, and a postmortem template.

Scope / Not in scope:
- In-situ model retraining or any model changes outside config-level routing (NOT scope).
- Full rewrite of the observability stack (out of scope; we will iterate on dashboards and alerts only).

SprintKit contents (what teams get):
- SLO spec templates (availability, p99 latency, request error rate) with example SLIs and query strings.
- Ops-bridge checklist: pre-shift readiness, escalation flow, on-call playbook excerpt.
- Mini-runbook generator: single-page runbook scaffold to populate per-service.
- Dashboard tuning checklist and suggested Prometheus/TraceQL queries.
- Canary recipe + rollback triggers for model-variant fallback.
- Postmortem skeleton and low-friction retro prompts.

Quick wins (first 7 days):
- T1: Publish SLO template and assign owners for 3 routes (owner assignment meeting Wed). Owner: Marcus Li (coord).
- T2: Apply dashboard tuning to reduce noise (Sofia G to push initial alert threshold changes).
- T3: Dry-run the ops-bridge checklist during week 1 on-call shift (Evelyn T to run exercise).

Cross-functional roles & responsibilities:
- Eng-SRE (Ayesha Patel): Sprint owner, SLO modelling, incident playbook edits, runbook review.
- Observability (Sofia Gomez): Dashboard queries, alert tuning, metrics instrumentation gaps.
- Platform/Serving (Daniel Okafor): Canary plumbing, routing policies, rollback automation.
- Product (owner TBD): Define user-impact SLO targets, acceptance criteria for canary.
- Solutions Eng / CS (Marcus Li): Customer communication post-canary, stakeholder updates.

High-level timeline (6-week pulse):
- Week 0 (Prep, 3 days): finalize SLO templates; identify service owners; update Confluence.
- Week 1 (Tune): dashboard/alert tuning; false positive triage; runbook dry-run.
- Week 2 (Canary prep): implement canary for model fallback in staging; define metrics & rollback gates.
- Week 3 (Canary run): 48h canary in US-WEST with traffic ramp; monitor error budget burn.
- Week 4 (Post-canary analysis): evaluate canary signals, finalize failover policy if stable.
- Week 5 (Onboard): onboard 2 product teams to ops-bridge checklist; complete runbooks.
- Week 6 (Retro + Next actions): publish retro, update SprintKit, propose next pulse.

SLO examples (to be filled per-service):
- text-gen.route.v1: availability SLO = 99.9% (30-day window), SLI = successful 200 responses / total requests; error budget = 43.2 min/month.
- chat-stream.route.v2: p99 latency SLO = <= 350ms (7-day rolling); SLI based on tail latency distribution sampled at gateway.
- embeddings.index: error-rate SLO = <= 0.5% (30-day); SLI excludes client-side malformed payloads.

Alert tuning guidance (common causes of noise):
- Alerts firing on low cardinality metrics without grouping by route/model leads to noisy pages. Add route/model label filters.
- Use sliding-window anomaly detection for exponential traffic growth instead of static thresholds.
- Reduce alert severity for known noisy infra signals; surface aggregated service-level alerts instead.

Ops-bridge checklist (short form):
- Pre-shift: confirm dashboard has green summary, error budget summary OK.
- If an alert triggers: ack in 5 min, annotate hypothesized impact (latency vs errors), escalate to platform after 15 min if no mitigation.
- Rollback decision: if canary meets two consecutive fail gates (error budget burn > x OR p99 > threshold), auto-roll back and page on-call.
- Post-incident: within 24 hours create incident stub and within 72 hours publish postmortem draft.

Dependencies & blockers:
- Missing route labels: several services do not emit route/model labels; Observability to identify and PR fixes (Sofia).
- Production traffic shaping: Platform needs a canary traffic router ready (blocked by infra PR #428).
- Product sign-off: final SLO targets require product acceptance by end of Week 0.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Q1: Do we standardize on 30-day windows for availability SLOs or allow 7/30/90 per-product needs? (decision owner: Product).
- Q2: What is the exact error-budget burn threshold that triggers automatic rollback during canary? Propose 20% in 48h window.
- Q3: Who is the official ops-bridge pager for weekend canaries? Need named backup.

Risk register (top-level):
- Risk: Canary causes customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: small traffic percentage, quick rollback automation, customer comms plan prepared.
- Risk: Alert tuning misses real regressions. Mitigation: keep one-high-severity correlation alert; run a 2-week post-tuning observation period.

Communication plan:
- Weekly Pulse email on Fridays summarizing error budget, canary progress, and open decisions. Owner: Marcus Li.
- Slack channel #reliability-pulse for async updates, use structured templates for status.
- Stakeholder sync (30m) every other Tuesday with product + CS + platform.

Acceptance criteria (end of pulse):
- Three routes have published SLO specs with owners.
- Ops-bridge checklist exercised by at least two teams and runbooks created.
- Canary completed and either promoted (auto-fallback policy accepted) or rolled back with clear findings.
- False-positive alerts reduced by >= 60% for top-10 noisy alerts.

Action items (immediate):
- A1: Marcus to schedule SLO owner meeting (due: 2026-09-17).
- A2: Sofia to run initial alert tuning sweep and list top-10 noisy alerts (due: 2026-09-20).
- A3: Daniel to unblock PR #428 or provide rollback plan (due: 2026-09-22).
- A4: Evelyn to run ops-bridge dry run during on-call (due: 2026-09-23).

Notes to self / loose ideas (brain-dump):
- Could ship a tiny "runbook generator" bot that inserts service name, SLOs, runbook owner into a template when given a Jira key. Low friction -> higher adoption.
- Consider experiment: weekly SLO office hours for product teams — 30-minute drop-in to iterate on targets.
- Metric to track adoption: # services with published runbooks / total critical services. Target 50% by end of Q4.

Appendix: quick checklist for service owners (copy-paste):
1) Fill SLO template in Confluence with target & owner.
2) Confirm route labels present in metrics.
3) Add one aggregated service-level alert and one latency tail alert.
4) Populate runbook scaffold and specify rollback steps.
5) Join ops-bridge dry-run and confirm pager handoff.

-- END --
